transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-18 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~49 mins | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Leo Chen (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Redwood Product), Eli Turner (Novus Head of ML), Sofia Gomez (Novus PM), Raj Patel (Novus DevOps), Dana Li (Novus DS)

Summary (auto): quick product walkthrough of Redwood Eval/Quality Monitoring features: building prompt sets, creating regression alerts, A/B comparisons and running evaluations via API and Console. Discussed pilot scope, security, and next steps.

00:00:02 Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me all right?
00:00:05 Eli: yes loud and clear, thanks Maya.
00:00:10 Maya: cool, so today Leo will run through the console and the Optimize recommendations, then we'll show the API quickstart and how you'd hook up prompt sets and regression alerts; we left time for Q&A and security questions at the end.
00:00:22 Leo: hi all, quick housekeeping: i'll be sharing my screen, if folks have access issues let us know.
00:00:31 Sofia: looks good on our side.
00:00:45 Leo: alright jumping in — Console home, per-route metrics, you can see token-level cost and latency, and the eval tab over here is where we manage prompt sets and tests.
00:01:10 Leo: (screen) here's an example prompt set we created for a finance use case — customer intake summary, balance predictions, and a policy response; each prompt has expected outputs and a suite of metrics: BLEU-ish, ROUGE-ish, and custom semantic similarity thresholds.
00:01:38 Dana: quick q — how do you store the expected outputs? is that encrypted at rest?
00:01:45 Leo: yes they're stored in the project's storage, encrypted with KMS; we also support customer-managed keys for Private deployments.
00:01:58 Maya: and we log eval runs to the audit trail for compliance.
00:02:06 Eli: good. can you run an actual regression alert example? that's a key ask for us.
00:02:12 Leo: sure, going to the alerts page — you can create an alert on any metric in the eval: e.g., semantic similarity drop below 0.82 or a sudden increase in hallucination score.
00:02:28 Leo: i'll simulate a run — running baseline (A) vs new model (B) — notice the dashboard shows A/B comparison and flags regressions automatically when thresholds are crossed.
00:02:48 Sofia: is the A/B comparison deterministic? we need to ensure same prompts match.
00:02:54 Leo: yes you pin the exact prompt set and random seeds; for larger batches we keep request metadata so you can do prompt-level diffs and sample-level traces.
00:03:10 Raj: is there an export for failing examples? our compliance folks want raw transcripts.
00:03:15 Leo: export of failing cases is supported as a CSV and JSONL, and you can push to your S3 or to a secure bucket in private.
00:03:25 Dana: how do you measure 'hallucination score' — machine metric or human-in-the-loop?
00:03:31 Leo: it's configurable — you can plug in model-based detectors, or use human labels; we surface both and allow you to set alerts on either signal.
00:03:44 Maya: for Optimize, we surface quantization suggestions and batching settings based on your prompt length distribution; this often gives a 20-40% cost reduction without much quality impact.
00:03:58 Eli: that sounds promising. what's the typical latency tradeoff with quantization?
00:04:04 Leo: depends on model and hardware — 4-bit quant can increase per-token latency slightly on some kernels but reduces memory pressure allowing higher throughput; in our console we show estimated latency/cost delta per profile.
00:04:23 Anika: we also recommend routing policies — e.g., use hosted for non-sensitive traffic and dedicated for regulated endpoints.
00:04:33 Sofia: ok on security: we need SOC2, SSO, and data residency in us-east-1.
00:04:40 Maya: we have SOC2 reports — i'll share them after, SSO via SAML is supported, and region pinning to us-east-1 is available for Dedicated and Private.
00:04:53 Raj: for Private deployment, does the control plane leave our VPC?
00:04:58 Leo: control plane can be customer-managed for Private, and for Dedicated we offer VPC peering; we can walk through architectures with your infra team.
00:05:10 Eli: excellent. moving to the API: can you show how we'd programmatically run an eval set?
00:05:17 Leo: sure — quickstart: call /v1/evals.create with the prompt set id, baseline model and candidate model, and the metrics you want; we'll return a job id, streaming results, and a finished report that you can query.
00:05:34 Leo: (typing) here's a curl snippet, and here's a python example in the notebook I'll push to your sandbox.
00:05:45 Dana: do we get token-level attribution in the results? we want to correlate tokens with cost.
00:05:50 Leo: yes response includes tokens consumed per request and a cost breakdown, plus per-prompt diffs.
00:06:05 Sofia: what about A/B significance testing — do you provide statistical tests?
00:06:10 Leo: yes built-in t-tests/bootstrapped CI for metrics, and we surface effect size with p-values; you can also export raw results for external analysis.
00:06:24 Eli: i'd like to see the CI on our critical intents.
00:06:29 Leo: we can configure per-intent thresholds and chain them into a composite alert.
00:06:40 Maya: quick qualification — what's your current eval workflow? how often do you run regressions, and who owns it?
00:06:47 Eli: right now it's ad-hoc — Dana runs a weekly eval and we manually compare diffs in notebooks; we don't have automated alerts.
00:06:57 Maya: understood — this should speed that up. pilot idea: run an automated weekly eval across your 3 critical intents and set regression alerts for semantic similarity and hallucination.
00:07:10 Sofia: timeline wise we want to decide in 2 weeks and pilot in July.
00:07:15 Maya: sounds reasonable.
00:07:18 Raj: any network requirements for Dedicated? we use strict egress controls.
00:07:24 Leo: Dedicated supports private networking and custom egress rules; we'll need to coordinate on firewall rules.
00:07:31 Raj: ok we'll share firewall rules.
00:07:36 Dana: question — can we run human-in-the-loop labeling inside the Eval console?
00:07:41 Leo: yes there's a labeling workflow; you can route failing cases to human label queues and ingest labels back into the eval.
00:07:52 Dana: nice.
00:08:05 Leo: demoing a regression alert configuration now — threshold, scope (intent subset), notification channels (Slack, webhook, email).
00:08:22 Sofia: will webhook payload include full output and metadata?
00:08:26 Leo: yes includes prompt id, prompt text, model outputs, metric values, and trace id.
00:08:36 Eli: we need redaction before sending to external webhooks.
00:08:40 Leo: you can configure redaction policies on a per-route basis.
00:08:48 Maya: okay i'm going to switch to the Optimize tab — these are recommended batching windows and quant profiles based on your observed distribution of sequence lengths.
00:09:02 Leo: we also recommend model variants for fallbacks — e.g., when latency spikes fallback to a lower-memory quant variant; that's part of graceful degradation.
00:09:15 Eli: what about cost forecasting?
00:09:18 Maya: Console has per-route cost projections and the Optimize tool can simulate cost for different batching/quant profiles.
00:09:26 Sofia: can we run a simulated monthly bill for our 500k monthly tokens?
00:09:31 Maya: yes we'll run that for the pilot and share a cost comparison: hosted vs dedicated with reserved capacity.
00:09:40 Raj: latency SLOs matter — what SLOs can we expect on Dedicated?
00:09:44 Leo: depends on commit level, but typical 95th percentile token latency targets are shown on the Dedicated plan page; for our customers we often hit sub-50ms per-token on A100-class hardware with optimizations.
00:09:59 Eli: good.
00:10:15 Leo: jumping back to API, here's how you'd schedule periodic evals via CRON and push results to your analytics pipeline via webhook.
00:10:25 Dana: would the webhook scale if we have thousands of failing cases?
00:10:30 Leo: webhooks are rate-limited; for high-volume we recommend S3 export + Athena or Kafka sink.
00:10:39 Sofia: any limits on prompt set size? we have a couple thousand test prompts.
00:10:44 Leo: prompt sets up to 100k items are supported but for interactive runs we sample; bulk evals are optimized for batch execution.
00:10:56 Maya: quick demo of the sample diff view — shows reference vs candidate with color-coded tokens and an aggregated metric rollup.
00:11:10 Leo: note the transcription may mislabel some tokens in auto-annotations — we flag low-confidence tokens for manual review.
00:11:24 Eli: sounds good.
00:11:30 Maya: moving to procurement questions — what's the billing model for pilot?
00:11:35 Leo: pilot is usage-based with a capped budget; if you move to Dedicated it's a reserved commit with monthly billing.
00:11:44 Sofia: for the pilot we want a 2-week run with representative traffic.
00:11:49 Maya: that's doable. we'll propose pricing in the follow-up.
00:11:55 Eli: any IP concerns around storing our prompts in Redwood?
00:11:59 Maya: data ownership stays with you; we don't claim IP on prompts or outputs in the contract. I'll include the clause in the docs.
00:12:10 Raj: let's talk SSO — we use Okta.
00:12:13 Maya: we support Okta / SAML; Leo will include SAML setup steps in the sandbox repo.
00:12:21 Leo: (note) will include a sample SAML metadata file.
00:12:30 Dana: question about drift detection — can you alert on distribution shift of token length?
00:12:36 Leo: yes we have data drift detectors and you can set alerts if distribution moves beyond threshold; they feed into Optimize suggestions too.
00:12:48 Eli: do you version evals? we need to maintain historical reports.
00:12:52 Leo: every eval run is versioned with model id, prompt set id, and commit sha; you can replay older runs too.
00:13:04 Sofia: is there an SDK for our infra team to integrate results?
00:13:09 Leo: yes python and go SDKs; we'll share the notebook.
00:13:18 Maya: quickly demoing the SDK snippet for running an eval and polling a job.
00:13:40 (screen) code shows eval.create, then eval.get_report(job_id) and how to parse metrics.
00:13:55 Dana: if a regression is detected can we auto-trigger a rollback?
00:13:59 Leo: we support webhook triggers to your deployment system; some customers set up auto-fallbacks when critical intent quality drops.
00:14:12 Eli: cautious about automatic rollback — prefer manual gating.
00:14:16 Maya: that's common; webhook can notify your CI and create a PR rather than do an auto-rollback.
00:14:25 Sofia: can you show a sample dashboard layout for the three intents we mentioned?
00:14:30 Leo: creating a custom dashboard now, pinning metric widgets for each intent and adding an alerts panel.
00:15:02 Leo: (scroll) you can also set escalation policies per alert.
00:15:12 Raj: for Dedicated we'll need an estimated infra cost.
00:15:17 Maya: we'll include a cost model in the follow-up comparing hosted vs reserved Dedicated capacity.
00:15:25 Eli: okay i'm going to hand it over to our security PM, Sofia, for questions.
00:15:30 Sofia: thanks — can you confirm data retention controls and purge workflows?
00:15:35 Leo: retention is configurable per-project; you can set auto-purge and have soft-delete windows for reviewing data before deletion.
00:15:47 Sofia: audit log retention?
00:15:50 Maya: audit logs are retained per your contract; for Private deployments logs can stay in your environment.
00:15:59 Sofia: good.
00:16:10 (ambient) brief cross-talk about node setup and kernel selection — Leo mentions kernel tuning for long context models.
00:16:30 Leo: demoing an A/B report now — shows metric deltas, CI, and example failing prompts with highlights.
00:16:55 Dana: can we annotate examples inside the UI and have that feed back to training pipelines?
00:17:01 Leo: yes annotations can be exported and we have integrations to common MLOps systems; we can also push labels to your training S3 bucket.
00:17:16 Maya: ok circling back to pilot scoping: we'll run 2-week pilot with 3 intents, automated weekly evals, regression alerts on semantic similarity and hallucination, and manual human review for failing cases.
00:17:35 Eli: agreed.
00:17:40 Maya: any outstanding blockers?
00:17:43 Raj: just confirmation on firewall rules and S3 access.
00:17:46 Maya: we'll follow up.
00:17:50 Sofia: can you include a sample SLA for Dedicated?
00:17:53 Maya: yes, included in follow-up.
00:18:00 Leo: wrapping up with the notebook push — i'll provision keys and the quickstart repo now.
00:18:08 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll share docs and price in the next 48 hours.
00:18:15 Eli: thanks, appreciate the walkthrough.
00:18:20 (meeting continues with deeper technical Q&A)
00:25:00 Leo: deeper dive — kernel selection specifics for quantized LLMs: we pick kernels by sequence length distribution and memory constraints. slight transcription note: sometimes we say 'KV cache' and it comes out as 'kay vee cache' in auto-captions.
00:30:10 Dana: can you run an example where the semantic sim drifts below threshold and triggers a Slack alert?
00:30:20 Leo: simulating now — here's the trigger, alert sent, and failing examples pushed to our review queue.
00:30:40 Sofia: nice.
00:34:55 Raj: follow-up infra question — do you require outbound access to redwood control plane for Dedicated?
00:35:01 Leo: for Dedicated there is an option for a private control plane; if you use our hosted control plane we'll need restricted outbound for metrics and control signals.
00:36:12 Eli: final note on governance — we need an IL5-style audit trail; can Redwood provide fine-grained logs?
00:36:20 Maya: yes fine-grained tracing and per-request audit logs are available; for the most sensitive customers we can increase retention and integrate with SIEM.
00:36:35 Sofia: great.
00:36:50 Maya: closing recap: 1) we'll send SOC2 + security package, 2) Leo will provision sandbox and notebook, 3) we'll send pilot pricing and plan, 4) Novus to share prompt sets and infra constraints.
00:37:12 Eli: action items noted.
00:37:20 Maya: any last questions?
00:37:25 Sofia: none.
00:37:28 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links and next steps.
00:37:32 Meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: occasional auto-captions mislabel acronyms and product names; some speaker labels were collapsed into generic 'Speaker 1' in the recording but corrected in this export where possible.
